column5: Numeric token spelling is retained without a source-length or host-word cap
Sized-literal width prefixes preserve exact semantics beyond host size without allocating from the declared width
Output-number folding uses exact limb storage with no semantic source-width or host-word cap
Packed constant allocation is governed by explicit storage-width and evaluation-work ceilings
Arbitrary-width based literals remain packed until a checked integer-only declaration or range consumer conversion
PackedLogic4 retains exact width signedness and X Z planes while canonical text includes every source bit
Low-word and integer_value consumers use checked known signed or unsigned conversion only at an explicitly scalar or resource-bounded boundary
Runtime packed values use host-addressable word vectors rather than a one-word semantic representation
Interpreter and LLVM flattened register planes retain every packed word through expressions dynamic selections O0 and O2 execution and cold or warm cache reuse
Integral real and time scalar conversion is intentionally bounded to the host scalar ABI while packed values remain vectorized
VPI packed descriptors and bit logic4 and logic9 vector formats carry every host-addressable bit and state plane without an arbitrary semantic width cap
The VPI integer format is a scalar 64-bit host format and wider values must use a vector format
Memory words retain exact arbitrary-width packed values and X Z planes through readmem writemem selects assignments input-port bridges malformed-input rollback and governed file work ceilings
VCD trace debugger callbacks mixed conversion and public C Tcl CLI views retain exact above-host-word values and X Z state
Object design library checkpoint and native-cache payloads round-trip exact literal text width signedness and X Z state while every packed cache-key word and state plane participates in identity
